title: Filling in for Roy Eldridge at Jimmy Ryan's
summary: In recent years he works occasionally at Jimmy Ryan's, substituting for Roy Eldridge, but declined a recent call because of health and eye problems.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Well Herman, in these last two or three years, then, since then, have you played at all? Do you take any dates?
Oh yes. I work down to Jimmy Ryan's quite often, when Roy Eldridge takes off.
Oh, you fill in for Roy.
Yeah, I fill in for Roy.
But you don't do it on a steady -- like if he goes away for a few weeks, do you go in for --
Yes, I have been there for a few weeks while he went to Europe, and whatnot. I stayed in there and took over for him, and everybody, including me, was very happy.

Yeah, he called me, you know he called me, and not too long ago, and I wasn't -- I didn't feel too good. I told him no, because well, I was kind of maybe -- feeling kind of bad too, because I had been to the hospital to see my doctor about the eyes, and this, that, and that business, and I wasn't doing too good. Because when you're walking out that night, and you come in that dark halls, and all that place, and where I was living then, man -- yipe!
Oh, yes, quite different. Different, man, oh man, you don't know.
